ghi_chu.mo_ta: Two ships in the bay have a carrack/caravel-style rig and high-sterned hulls. They look like 15th–16th century vessels.
ghi_chu.ly_do: In 1779 the bay held full-rigged ships, frigates, xebecs and gunboats, including those of the Great Siege. These archaic rigs would be out of date by about 200 years.

ghi_chu.mo_ta: The foreground is an empty pastoral isthmus with tents, a wooden shed, cattle and low walls. The hill on the left is not the Rock of Gibraltar. There is no town, no Line Wall and no North Front fortifications.
ghi_chu.ly_do: In 1779 Gibraltar was a heavily fortified British garrison under Spanish siege. It had a walled town, batteries, and Spanish siege lines across the isthmus. The Rock has a very different profile.
